subject: civics
question_text: Which of the following sentiments about the reason for conducting elections are false?

mcq_options.option_text: Elections enable people to judge the performance of the government.
People select the representative of their choice in an election.
Elections enable people to evaluate the performance of the judiciary.
People can indicate which policies they prefer.

answer_text: Elections enable people to evaluate the performance of the judiciary.

subject: civics
question_text: Which of these is not a good reason to say that Indian elections are democratic?

mcq_options.option_text: India has the largest numbers of voters in the world.
India’s election commission is very powerful.
In India, everyone above the age of 18 has a right to vote.
In India, the losing parties accept the electoral verdict.

answer_text: India has the largest numbers of voters in the world.
final_answer: Therefore, option (a) is not a good reason.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of information regarding democratic elections.

question_text: Describe what Surekha should focus on for each of the following stages of election: Election campaign, Polling day, Counting day.

subject: civics
question_text:
Can we draw the following conclusions from the information given in this chapter? Give two facts to support your position for each of these.
a. Election Commission of India does not have enough powers to conduct free and fair elections in the country.
b. There is a high level of popular participation in the elections in our country.
c. It is very easy for the party in power to win an election.
d. Many reforms are needed to make our elections completely free and fair.

parts.part_text: Election Commission of India does not have enough powers to conduct free and fair elections in the country.
parts.answer_text: It is wrong to say that election commission of India does not have enough powers to conduct free and fair elections. Because Election Commission of India have enough powers to conduct free and fair elections in the country. The Election Commission of India is an independent and powerful body.

steps.description: State the powers of the Election Commission.
Explain the appointment and removal of the Election Commissioner.
Mention the authority to order repoll if elections are not conducted fairly.
Highlight that other government servants work under the control of the Election Commissioner during elections.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, the Election Commission has sufficient powers to ensure free and fair elections.

parts.part_text: There is a high level of popular participation in the elections in our country.
parts.answer_text: It is a fact that there is a high level of popular participation in the elections in our country. During the last 50 years or so, the turn out of voters in the North America and Europe has declined while in India it has either remained stable or increased.

steps.description: Compare voter turnout in India with that in North America and Europe.
Mention the participation of different socio-economic groups in voting.

parts.final_answer: Thus, popular participation in Indian elections is significant and increasing.

parts.part_text: It is very easy for the party in power to win an election.
parts.answer_text: It is quite a wrong notion that party in power can win an election quite easily in India. If such a thing would have been true, the Congress stalwart like Indira Gandhi, the then Prime Minister of India, would not have been defeated by Raj Narain.

steps.description: Provide an example of a significant political defeat.
Mention other occasions when ruling parties have lost elections.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, it is not easy for the ruling party to win elections in India.

parts.part_text: Many reforms are needed to make our elections completely free and fair.
parts.answer_text: There is no system as such where can not be a reform and improvement. Reforms are required to prevent use of money, muscle power, and unfair practices from bearing fruit.

steps.description: State the need for reforms in the electoral system.
Identify specific areas where reforms are necessary.

parts.final_answer: Thus, reforms are essential for ensuring free and fair elections.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of electoral processes and the implications of various statements.

subject: civics
question_text: Chinappa was convicted for torturing his wife for dowry. Satbir was held guilty of practicing untouchability. The court did not allow either of them to contest elections. Does this decision go against the principles of democratic elections?
answer_text: In both the cases, Chinappa and Satbir, the court has done the right thing by not allowing either of them to contest elections. This decision does not go against the principle of democratic elections.
final_answer: Therefore, the decision to disallow them from contesting elections upholds democratic principles.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding the implications of legal decisions on democracy.

subject: civics
question_text:
Here are some reports of electoral malpractices from different parts of the world. Is there anything that these countries can learn from India to improve their elections? What would you suggest in each case?
(a) During an election in Nigeria, the officer-in-charge of counting votes deliberately increased the votes of one candidate and declared him elected.
(b) Just before the elections in Fiji, a pamphlet was distributed warning voters that a vote for former Prime Minister, Mahendra Chaudhry will lead to bloodshed.
(c) In the US, each state has its own method of voting, its own procedure of counting and its own authority for conducting elections.

mcq_options.option_text: During an election in Nigeria, the officer-in-charge of counting votes deliberately increased the votes of one candidate and declared him elected.
Just before the elections in Fiji, a pamphlet was distributed warning voters that a vote for former Prime Minister, Mahendra Chaudhry will lead to bloodshed.
In the US, each state has its own method of voting, its own procedure of counting and its own authority for conducting elections.

parts.part_text: During an election in Nigeria, the officer-in-charge of counting votes deliberately increased the votes of one candidate and declared him elected.
parts.answer_text: The officer-in-charge during elections (counting) should have been impartial and should have ordered repoll. For voting there should be electronic machines so that no fraud could be done in counting.

steps.description: State the need for impartiality in vote counting.
Suggest the use of electronic voting machines to prevent fraud.

parts.final_answer: Thus, Nigeria can learn from India about ensuring transparency in vote counting.

parts.part_text: Just before the elections in Fiji, a pamphlet was distributed warning voters that a vote for former Prime Minister, Mahendra Chaudhry will lead to bloodshed.
parts.answer_text: Such a thing is quite wrong against the spirit of a free and fair election. Voters should never be threatened to cast their vote against their conscience.

steps.description: Emphasize the importance of a free and fair election.
Suggest that any pamphlet should be distributed well in advance of the election.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, Fiji can learn from India not to intimidate voters.

parts.part_text: In the US, each state has its own method of voting, its own procedure of counting and its own authority for conducting elections.
parts.answer_text: In India, one and uniform rules are followed in all states as far as the method of voting, procedure of counting are concerned.

steps.description: Highlight the uniformity of electoral procedures in India.
Point out the issues caused by different rules in the US.

parts.final_answer: Thus, the US can take lessons from India on maintaining uniform electoral procedures.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires analysis of electoral practices and understanding of democratic principles.

subject: civics
question_text:
Here are some reports of malpractices in Indian elections. Identify what the problem in each case is. What should be done to correct the situation?
(a) Following the announcement of elections the minister promised to provide financial aid to reopen the closed sugar mill.
(b) Opposition parties alleged that their statements and campaign was not given the due attention in Doordarshan and All India Radio.
(c) An inquiry by the Election Commission showed that electoral rolls of a state contain names of 20 lakh fake voters.
(d) The hoodlums of a political party were moving with guns, physically preventing supporters of other political parties to meet the voters and attacking meetings of other parties.

mcq_options.option_text: Following the announcement of elections the minister promised to provide financial aid to reopen the closed sugar mill.
Opposition parties alleged that their statements and campaign was not given the due attention in Doordarshan and All India Radio.
An inquiry by the Election Commission showed that electoral rolls of a state contain names of 20 lakh fake voters.
The hoodlums of a political party were moving with guns, physically preventing supporters of other political parties to meet the voters and attacking meetings of other parties.

parts.part_text: Following the announcement of elections the minister promised to provide financial aid to reopen the closed sugar mill.
parts.answer_text: By doing so, the minister has erred on two counts. Firstly, he should not have made this promise when the announcement of elections has already been made. Secondly, by promising financial aid he is trying to bribe the voters by using financial tricks.

steps.description: Identify the inappropriate timing of the promise.
Explain the implications of bribing voters.

parts.final_answer: Thus, the minister's actions should be condemned and the promise should not be fulfilled.

parts.part_text: Opposition parties alleged that their statements and campaign was not given the due attention in Doordarshan and All India Radio.
parts.answer_text: In order to remove this allegation of the opposition parties, the best solution is that Doordarshan and All India Radio must be made autonomous bodies so that government could not influence them in its favour.

steps.description: Propose making media outlets autonomous.
Suggest equal airtime for all parties.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, ensuring media autonomy is crucial for fair elections.

parts.part_text: An inquiry by the Election Commission showed that electoral rolls of a state contain names of 20 lakh fake voters.
parts.answer_text: The presence of fake voters undermines the integrity of the electoral process. Immediate action should be taken to update and verify the electoral rolls.

steps.description: Identify the problem of fake voters.
Suggest actions to update electoral rolls.

parts.final_answer: Thus, verifying electoral rolls is essential for maintaining electoral integrity.

parts.part_text: The hoodlums of a political party were moving with guns, physically preventing supporters of other political parties to meet the voters and attacking meetings of other parties.
parts.answer_text: Such actions are a direct threat to democracy and must be dealt with severely. Law enforcement should ensure the safety of all political parties and their supporters.

steps.description: Highlight the threat posed by political violence.
Propose measures for law enforcement to protect democratic processes.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, strict action against political violence is necessary to uphold democracy.

difficulty_reasoning: Involves critical analysis of electoral malpractices and proposing solutions.

subject: civics
question_text: Ramesh was not in class when this chapter was being taught. He came the next day and reported what he had heard from his father. Can you tell Ramesh what is wrong with these statements?

parts.part_text: Women always vote the way men tell them. So what is the point of giving them the right to vote?
parts.answer_text: Women always vote the way men tell them to do is a wrong statement. It would be totally undemocratic if we debar women who are about 50 per cent of the population, of their right to vote on the basis of gender distinction. It will also take away the quality of true representation of a democracy. Often we see husband contesting election from one party while his wife contesting from another party.
parts.final_answer: Thus, denying women the right to vote based on the assumption that they follow men's decisions undermines democracy.

parts.part_text: Party politics creates tension in society. Elections should be decided by consensus not by competition.
parts.answer_text: A healthy competition provides option to the people to choose the better. A consensus can make the people deaf and dumb which is against the spirit of democracy. Electoral competition is necessary because it provides incentives to political parties and leaders and forces them to serve the people better.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, competition in elections is essential for a vibrant democracy.

parts.part_text: Only graduates should be allowed to stand as candidates for elections.
parts.answer_text: Educational qualifications are not necessary to all kinds of jobs. It is also a wrong notion that only graduates should be allowed to contest elections. A majority of people who fought for the independence of the country were almost illiterate. They have equal right with those of the educated to enjoy the fruit of the hard won independence. It is also agreed that if a graduate degree is made an eligibility criteria, then more than 90% of the voters would become ineligible for contesting an election. Would that be a democracy, certainly not. India follows the rule – ‘One person one vote’. This is in true spirit of democracy.
parts.final_answer: Thus, restricting candidacy to graduates contradicts the democratic principle of equal representation.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of democratic principles and the implications of electoral policies.
